small_guidance:
- The conv now dominates (~all of 6.69ms). Tuning the pool/LSE/ReLU kernel further is unlikely to move the needle; instead, ensure the conv runs in channels_last_3d memory format (`x.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d)` and convert weight similarly in `__init__`) to let cuDNN pick faster kernels.
- If keeping the current pool kernel, add larger TILE configs (64, 128) with num_warps=8 to reduce launch/program overhead since each program already does cheap work per output element.
- Consider fusing the bias add of conv into the pool kernel by using `nn.Conv3d(..., bias=False)` and adding bias inside the LSE kernel, eliminating one pass over the post-conv tensor.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton implicit-GEMM conv3d kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output spatial tile), gather input via computed offsets (im2col implicit), and fuse bias. This is the biggest headroom since conv now is ~100% of runtime.
- Even better: fuse the entire pipeline — conv3d + 2x2x2 maxpool + channel LSE + ReLU — into one kernel that emits the (N,1,Do,Ho,Wo) tensor directly, by tiling over output-pool-spatial and looping over OC inside the program (accumulating max over the 8 conv outputs per channel, then LSE-reducing across channels). This avoids materializing the full (N,64,D,H,W) conv output (~128MB).
- If a single mega-kernel is too complex, do conv3d→maxpool fusion as one Triton kernel (writing pooled output of shape (N,64,Do,Ho,Wo), 16x smaller), then keep the existing LSE/ReLU kernel on that smaller tensor.
